source_quote: Is there any way that we can speak to what remained of him, even though they don't have all their parts? I mean, we don't need the heart — we just need the brain to be able to talk to him, you know.

subject: Tiamat
fact: Tiamat was denied her power because a dwarf chose — cited by the Stroudite school as evidence of sovereign mortal choice.
source_quote: Tiamat was denied her power because a dwarf chose.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth is a scholar who formalizes theological frameworks around Stroudite and Bahamutian schools, names them the strong-weak hypothesis, and is meticulous in filing ideas — he also recites and explains Candlekeep’s prophecy system with pedagogical care.
source_quote: Vareth calls it a compromise of the Bahamutian school... He names this the strong-weak hypothesis with the satisfaction of a man who has just filed something correctly.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth is a scholar with forty-one years in the West Inner Ward of Candlekeep, who navigates institutional gravity and knows which way to lean into it.
source_quote: Brother Vareth moves through it like a man who has been navigating institutional gravity for forty-one years and knows which way to lean into it.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth is a senior librarian at Candlekeep who has maintained his side office for forty-one years, known for institutional restraint and deep engagement with theological debates, and recently developed a new theory about fixed points in mortal agency.
source_quote: He has been keeping this corner of the library for forty-one years, he says, and he knows what a fashion looks like.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth is an aging scholar with forty-one years in a side office at Candlekeep, deeply immersed in theological disputes, who unexpectedly adopted and refined a new school of thought — the Grygum school — after an offhand remark by the narrator, and is now actively researching it with renewed passion.
source_quote: He is articulating the theory back to me now — someone had to arrive at a particular point, and at that point their choices were constrained, but who would arrive there was unconstrained — and I am nodding because yes, that is exactly it.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth names the Grygum school a compromise of the Bahamutian school and labels the narrator a weak Stroudite and a weak Bahamutian, calling it the strong-weak hypothesis.
source_quote: He calls it a compromise of the Bahamutian school. He calls me a weak Stroudite — a strong Stroudite holds there are no fixed points at all — and a strong Bahamutian around fixed points, and a weak Bahamutian outside of them. He names this the strong-weak hypothesis with the satisfaction of a man who has just filed something correctly.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a dragonborn with exceptional attention to detail; he analyzed the wound pattern on Janussi’s body and concluded the rib cage was shattered by multiple axe blows, the heart removed post-mortem, and the blood spatter inconsistent with a violent death; he supported the theory that the heart was removed to prevent resurrection.
source_quote: The rib cage had been smashed by something like an axe, multiple blows, close together, deliberate.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a half-orc who quietly questions whether the cat is truly just a cat, triggering a moment of doubt in Fembris and revealing his own suspicion.
source_quote: Is it?

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is analyzing the architecture and layout of Candlekeep with tactical precision, noting exits, traffic patterns, and structural dominance; he is cataloging surface-world features as potential assets or threats after prolonged time in the Underdark.
source_quote: Exits: three visible archways, one service passage, one guarded door to the north. Foot traffic: light, scholars moving in pairs, nobody moving fast. No elevated positions. No obvious coverage points.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced as the one patiently teaching Glabbagool, the grey ooze, to formalize monastic discipline.
source_quote: Whatever Glabbagool had been doing in the bag all day — thinking, absorbing, trying to formalize whatever Zalthir had been patiently teaching him into monastic discipline...

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is the head and founder of the Grygumite School, and arrived at the Chapter House as an uninvited guest, observed and categorized by the Council of Twelve as an unknown arrival with no provenance.
source_quote: I am the head of the Grygumite School. Founder, in fact.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir observed that the rib cage had been smashed by multiple close, deliberate blows from something like an axe, the heart was missing, and the blood was localized — indicating a pattern inconsistent with a violent death and suggesting the wound was insufficient to cause death.
source_quote: The rib cage had been smashed by something like an axe, multiple blows, close together, deliberate. The heart was missing. No other organs. And the blood was localized.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir says, very quietly, 'Is it?'
source_quote: Is it?

subject: Zuggtmoy
fact: Zuggtmoy is referenced in marginalia and theological documents as a deity whose influence is subtly embedded in the architecture of belief, including the Lolth/Zuggtmoy equivalence.
source_quote: The Zuggtmoy marginalia. The theological document from Asha Vandree's chain mail — the Lolth/Zuggtmoy equivalence...

subject: Asha Vandree's chain mail document
fact: A theological document sewn into Asha Vandree's chain mail asserts a Lolth/Zuggtmoy equivalence, written in a hand designed to appear incidental.
source_quote: The theological document from Asha Vandree's chain mail — the Lolth/Zuggtmoy equivalence, written in a hand that wanted very much to seem incidental.

subject: Astronomicon value
fact: The Astronomicon is a stack of blue globes ascending in scale, containing everything known about the stars.
source_quote: You see that curious blue stack of globes? That's the Astronomicon. Everything we know about the stars can be found there

subject: bag of holding
fact: The bag of holding was used to confine Glabbagool the grey ooze for most of the day — an act now understood as technically fine but genuinely unkind, akin to keeping a puppy in a closet during a thunderstorm.
source_quote: The grey ooze had been confined to the bag of holding for most of the day, which in hindsight was probably like keeping a puppy in a closet during a thunderstorm

subject: candelabra

source_quote: The candelabra — seven arms, bronze — had burned its candles entirely to wax puddles.

subject: Candelabra
fact: A seven-armed bronze candelabra has burned all seven candles to wax puddles, confirming the room remained sealed for many hours after death; the candles’ complete consumption contradicts housekeeper Hollypocket’s standards.
source_quote: The candelabra — seven arms, bronze — had burned its candles entirely to wax puddles.

source_quote: The candelabra — seven arms, bronze — had burned its candles entirely to wax puddles.

fact: A bronze candelabra with seven arms, all candles completely burned down to wax puddles. Its state confirms the room remained sealed for many hours after death, as the candles would not have been allowed to burn out under normal protocol.
source_quote: The candelabra — seven arms, bronze — had burned its candles entirely to wax puddles.

subject: Confidentiality Papers
fact: The confidentiality papers are the formal requirement imposed by the Council before the investigation may proceed. They are a tool of control, designed to limit the scope of inquiry and bind the investigators to institutional silence.
source_quote: Confidentiality papers first.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sword housed in a scabbard, claimed by the party to have been found in a tomb after two thousand years. Its presence is used rhetorically to assert their legendary status and justify their claim to be the greatest discoverers.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sword housed in its scabbard that claimed to have been found in a tomb after two thousand years.
source_quote: Dawnbringer, housed in her scabbard, took the opportunity to note that we must surely be the greatest discoverers of all, having found her tomb after two thousand years.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a weapon left against the wall within reach in the Refectory, its placement having been the subject of a prolonged negotiation; it is neither drawn nor secured, reflecting a state of cautious readiness.

subject: Dawnbringer

subject: Dawnbringer

subject: Ilvara's prayer book

subject: Ilvara's prayer book

source_quote: A wicker basket nearby holding a linen ink carrier, slightly damp, which had been the vessel for the ink now pooling from the spilled pot.

subject: Ink Pot and Quill

subject: Janussi's heart

subject: Midnight Blue Ink Notes
fact: A pile of recent notes on Janussi's research, written in midnight blue ink and pinned under a quartz weight. These notes were the freshest, indicating his most recent work. A quill with the same ink was found on the floor, suggesting he was actively writing before death.
source_quote: To the other side, a larger pile of notes pinned under a quartz weight, with more annotations on top in midnight blue ink — and below those, older notes in purple.

subject: missing heart

source_quote: The heart was missing. No other organs. And the blood was localized. Wrong pattern for what should have been a violent death.

subject: notes

subject: Pizwog's research tract

subject: Poirot and Colombo references
fact: The references to Poirot and Colombo are narrative tools invoked by Thorin and the group to legitimize their investigative methods. They serve as cultural shorthand for deductive reasoning and are used to counter institutional skepticism.
source_quote: We were students of the great Masters Poirot and Colombo.

subject: Prophecies in the gallery
fact: Prophecies are recited from the gallery above the Refectory, originating from Alaundo, and are removed when fulfilled; what remains is the unfulfilled inventory.
source_quote: The prophecies had been going the whole time, floating down from the gallery above like water finding its level. Vareth had explained it to Grygum earlier in the day... there was a man named Alaundo whose prophecies had come true with uncomfortable regularity, so Candlekeep had been reciting them ever since. Whenever one came true, it was removed. What remained was the unfulfilled inventory.

subject: Prophecy: 'On the longest night of winter's deepest cold, the keeper falls, the heart is sold.'
fact: A prophecy recited from the gallery — 'On the longest night of winter's deepest cold, the keeper falls, the heart is sold.' — lands with the narrator and is kept silent.
source_quote: *On the longest night of winter's deepest cold, the keeper falls, the heart is sold.* It landed. I sat with it for a second.

subject: Purple Ink Notes

subject: The cat

source_quote: Gray. Motionless. Yellow eyes that opened the moment we got close. The cat had decided it need not move for anyone, and tracked us anyway.

subject: The Golden Ass

subject: The Golden Ass

source_quote: why isn't Sylvira Savikas here?

subject: Ajar door on third floor
fact: The third-floor apartment’s door was left open despite the crime scene lockdown; its purpose, contents, and connection to the murder are unknown and unexamined.
source_quote: A large apartment at the third with its door left conspicuously ajar.

subject: ajar third-floor door
fact: The third-floor apartment door is left open, unexamined, and the cat is frequently observed nearby; the apartment may contain the missing book, the killer’s trace, or a hidden ritual site.
source_quote: A large apartment at the third with its door left conspicuously ajar.

subject: Architectural manipulation of belief
fact: It is theorized that a god seeking to control mortal outcomes would not compel actions directly, but would shape the architecture of evidence, polemic, and institutional space to guide belief.
source_quote: A god who wished to control the outcome of mortal lives would not need to compel a single hand. She would only need to shape the rules of the evidence. The form of polemic. The architecture of a chapter house.

subject: Bookwyrm’s alibi
fact: Bookwyrm claimed she had nothing to do with Janussi’s death when directly questioned by Thorin. Her pause before answering was deliberate. Daz noted her expression, but did not record it. Her testimony is now under suspicion, and her knowledge of Janussi’s final request suggests she may have been involved in the events leading to his death — or in covering them up.

subject: Bookwyrm’s denial
fact: Bookwyrm’s emphatic denial — 'I had nothing to do with it' — is a thread of ambiguity. Her pause before speaking, and the timing of her revelation, suggest concealment or guilt. The investigators are now aware she is a suspect.
source_quote: I can assure you, I had nothing to do with it.

subject: Bookwyrm's possible involvement
fact: Bookwyrm’s claim that she had nothing to do with Janussi’s death is unverified and suspicious.
source_quote: Bookwyrm paused. ... 'I can assure you, I had nothing to do with it.'

subject: cat's nature
fact: The gray cat with yellow eyes exhibits unnatural awareness, tracks investigators without moving, and has been the subject of theological debate — whether it is a familiar, a shapeshifter, or a sentient entity; Bookwyrm’s fear and Fembris’s reconsideration suggest it is more than it seems.
source_quote: Nobody had been able to conclusively prove the cat was some kind of power that lived here, and nobody had been able to conclusively prove that it was not.

subject: corpse accessibility
fact: The corpse of Janussi cannot be contacted again via ritual for some time, meaning any future attempt must wait until the cooldown period has passed, or until it is confirmed no prior ritual had already been spent.
source_quote: Once performed, the same corpse cannot be reached again for some time.

subject: Disappearance of The Golden Ass
fact: The book Janussi was most recently annotating — The Golden Ass — is missing. Its absence suggests it contained critical information the thief wanted to suppress or possess, and it was removed deliberately after the murder.
source_quote: Whatever Janussi had been working on most recently, writing about in the freshest ink, on the most recent night of his life, was gone.

subject: Fourth school of thought
fact: A fourth school of thought has been proposed — that fixed points constrain mortal agency near them, while freedom exists between them, and the universe becomes conspiratorially silent in service of invariance.
source_quote: But… but what if there's a fourth? What if there are certain fixed points around which our actions must revolve? And the closer we come to one of those fixed points, the more constrained we are, but between them, perhaps we have a great deal of freedom of action.

subject: Gate Warden's discovery
fact: The Gate Warden found something during his inspection that made him leave the chamber more determined — possibly evidence of the killer’s identity, the location of the missing book, or confirmation of the heart’s ritual purpose; he was removed before being questioned.
source_quote: He definitely looked more determined after he walked out.

subject: Gate Warden’s hidden discovery
fact: The Gate Warden conducted a private inspection and emerged with increased determination, suggesting he found something incriminating or unexpected before being removed from the investigation — his report to the Council remains unshared.
source_quote: Tadric noted that Kalan looked more determined coming out than going in. The Gate Warden again at eleven, alone, for a full inspection — careful, deliberate, left to make his report to the Council.

subject: Identity of the Murderer
fact: The murderer likely had access to the Keeper’s chambers, knowledge of his research, and the ability to remain undetected for hours. The deliberate sealing of the room, the specific removal of an object from the chest, and the theft of The Golden Ass suggest a targeted assassination, not a robbery.
source_quote: That felt deliberate in the way that things feel deliberate when you stop trying to find an innocent explanation for them.

subject: inventory of unfulfilled prophecies
fact: Candlekeep maintains an inventory of unfulfilled prophecies — the collection of Alaundo’s unmet predictions — and no one knows what happens when the inventory runs out.
source_quote: Nobody knew what happened when the inventory ran out.

subject: Kalan’s removal
fact: Kalan was relieved of duty before being questioned, and his demeanor upon leaving suggests he may have witnessed or done something that made his continued presence a risk.
source_quote: Tadric noted that Kalan looked more determined coming out than going in.

subject: Kalan’s resignation request
fact: The request for Kalan Strongbranch’s resignation, issued by Janussi the morning of his death, is an unresolved thread that may be motive, red herring, or key to the murder. It is the only documented interpersonal conflict preceding the death.
source_quote: Janussi asked Kalan to tender his resignation.

subject: missing heart
fact: The removal of Janussi’s heart was not for theft but to prevent resurrection; the killer anticipated magical intervention and acted to ensure permanent death; this implies knowledge of arcane law and ritual limitations.
source_quote: They wanted Janussi to stay dead in every sense that mattered.

subject: Missing Object from Chest
fact: An object was removed from Janussi’s chest after death. Its nature is unknown, but its removal was intentional and preceded the theft of The Golden Ass. It is likely tied to his research and of greater value than gemstones.
source_quote: There was a hollow in his chest where something used to be.

subject: resurrection prevention
fact: The removal of Janussi's heart was not an act of mutilation but a deliberate measure to ensure he could not be resurrected, implying the perpetrator had knowledge of necromantic requirements.
source_quote: They wanted Janussi to stay dead in every sense that mattered.

subject: the Avowed’s silence
fact: The Avowed were asleep during the murder and have not yet been questioned. Their member’s death in the Dragon Breath Simulation Chamber suggests prior exposure to lethal magic. Their absence from the investigation may indicate complicity, fear, or institutional isolation. Their dormancy is suspicious.

subject: The cat’s true nature
fact: The cat’s behavior and the conflicting interpretations of its identity — from mundane animal to interdimensional entity — suggest it may be a key witness, a magical artifact, or a trap; its role is unresolved.
source_quote: Nobody had been able to conclusively prove the cat was some kind of power that lived here, and nobody had been able to conclusively prove that it was not.

subject: the Drakonoikos’s hidden archives
fact: The Drakonoikos, built from a dragon’s remains, may contain concealed archives or magical inscriptions. Its design suggests it was not merely symbolic but functional — perhaps housing knowledge that could explain Janussi’s fear, Kalan’s decline, or the nature of the threat that led to the murder. It has not yet been accessed by investigators.

subject: the emerald door
fact: The emerald door is a restricted passage used only for urgent, clandestine access — its invocation implies the Keeper’s death is tied to a hidden, possibly forbidden, layer of Candlekeep’s knowledge or architecture.
source_quote: Now, through the emerald door, before the avowed awake!

subject: The Grygum school of thought
fact: The Grygum school of thought was proposed accidentally and is now being treated as the question of the age.
source_quote: The Grygum school of thought. Filed under: things that started as offhand remarks.

subject: the hooded Avowed figure
fact: A hooded figure from the Avowed passed through the Refectory at a half-run, clutching something under their robe — not trying to hide it, yet not trying to be obvious — suggesting a covert transfer of evidence or contraband tied to the Keeper’s death.
source_quote: A hooded figure from the Avowed went past the dining hall at a half-run, something tucked against their ribs under the robe.

subject: the inventory of unfulfilled prophecies
fact: Candlekeep maintains an inventory of unfulfilled prophecies from Alaundo; when one comes true, it is removed — but no one knows what happens when the inventory runs out, implying a hidden threshold beyond which reality itself may unravel.
source_quote: Whenever one came true, it was removed. What remained was the unfulfilled inventory. Nobody knew what happened when the inventory ran out.

subject: the keeper falls, the heart is sold
fact: A prophecy descended from the gallery: 'On the longest night of winter's deepest cold, the keeper falls, the heart is sold.' It landed with weight; Grygum and Daz observed it silently, choosing not to react aloud.
source_quote: *On the longest night of winter's deepest cold, the keeper falls, the heart is sold.*

subject: The missing observation
fact: Tadric admits he was not observing, only controlling access — creating a critical blind spot in the timeline, especially regarding who entered or exited during the Gate Warden’s inspection.
source_quote: His assignment had been crowd control. Not observation.

subject: the missing resignation order
fact: Janussi’s request for Kalan’s resignation was delivered verbally, and no written record was produced. Bookwyrm declined to elaborate on the nature of his negligence. The absence of documentation raises the possibility that the order was fabricated — or that someone destroyed it after the murder to obscure motive.

subject: the nature of the Drakonoikos
fact: The Drakonoikos is mentioned as the next landmark in the tour but not described; its function, significance, and potential danger are unknown, making it a looming mystery in the narrative.
source_quote: Then the Drakonoikos.

subject: the prophecy: 'The keeper falls, the heart is sold'
fact: A prophecy recited in Candlekeep’s gallery — 'On the longest night of winter's deepest cold, the keeper falls, the heart is sold' — has just been fulfilled by the death of the Keeper of Tomes, suggesting the prophecy system is active, predictive, and possibly manipulative.
source_quote: *On the longest night of winter's deepest cold, the keeper falls, the heart is sold.* It landed.

subject: the unspoken protection of the library
fact: The Council’s reluctance to grant full access suggests they are protecting something within the library — perhaps evidence, a secret, or a person. The investigators have realized the murder has exposed institutional vulnerability, and the request for carte blanche has landed harder than the crime itself.
source_quote: We had just asked for something they had not realized they were protecting, and the request had landed harder than the murder.

subject: the wall is just a rock in the right place
fact: A metaphor from the giants — 'a wall is just a rock in the right place' — was privately applied by the speaker to prophecies: 'a prophecy that hasn't happened yet is just a warning waiting for its moment.' It was not spoken aloud, as it was deemed not useful.
source_quote: The giants used to say that a wall is just a rock in the right place. A prophecy that hasn't happened yet is just a warning waiting for its moment. I didn't say that out loud. It wasn't useful.

subject: the Zuggtmoy/Lolth equivalence
fact: The theological document hidden in Asha Vandree’s chain mail, equating Lolth with Zuggtmoy, was written in a hand designed to appear incidental — evidence of a hidden, institutionalized effort to merge or obscure two powerful entities within the church’s doctrine.
source_quote: The theological document from Asha Vandree's chain mail — the Lolth/Zuggtmoy equivalence, written in a hand that wanted very much to seem incidental.

subject: Thorin's request for ice
fact: Thorin asked about ice, but the availability or source of ice is not specified in this session.
source_quote: Is there any ice around?

subject: Thorin's wife
fact: Thorin's wife is referenced as having watched Poirot with him, but her identity and presence are unexplained.
source_quote: Thorin noted that he and his wife had been watching a great deal of Poirot lately.

subject: unauthorized access to the Chapter House
fact: Zalthir’s presence in the Chapter House raises a thread of suspicion — who granted him access, and does that reflect a deeper breach in the Council’s security or hierarchy?
source_quote: who gave you access, and should I object to them.

subject: why the First Reader chose this party
fact: The First Reader has bypassed all standard authorities to summon this specific group; the reason for her trust in them — and not the Avowed or city watch — remains unexplained and is a critical unresolved question.
source_quote: The question of why she thought that was, I noted, a question I would need answered.
